summary: 1949 L-4 cab on a 10-foot concrete base, after a 1929 D-6 cupola; staffed in summers; drive-up by gravel road in the Umatilla NF.

facts.design: L-4 cab on a 10-foot concrete base (1949); the site's first lookout was a D-6 cupola cabin (1929)

access.note: Summit reached by road: gravel FR 64, then FR-475, which may be gated. Working Forest Service lookout; these sources do not describe the cab's interior.

visit.trail_note: WillhiteWeb lists the distance as drive-up or 0.5 miles; a restroom sits near the lookout.

events.note: First structure on the summit: a D-6 cupola cabin; sources say it survived into the late 1950s
Present L-4 cab on a 10-foot concrete base
October 1930 story, reprinted online: lookout reported a fire near Lewis Peak on August 22; a cooperator crew was loaded in 39 minutes
Frank Hohenadel listed as lookout personnel; the source gives the span as 194? to 1965
Cab remodeled: knotty pine interior, new insulation, thermopane windows; metal shutters added
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, January 3, 2015

corrections.why: The sources describe a 10-foot concrete base under the L-4 cab and give no total tower height; the 3.0 m in the record matches the base, not the tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com says staffed 'every summer', WillhiteWeb says 'manned nearly every summer', TrailChick says 'usually staffed every year'; the 2019 register visit says 'Staffed in summer by FS'. The story uses the summer wording.

sources.title: Table Rock Lookout - Umatilla National Forest

notes_for_editor: Dates agree across sources: D-6 cupola 1929, L-4 cab 1949, cab remodel 1989, NHLR registration 2015. The brief's height_m 3.0 is the concrete base, not the tower; see corrections. Frank Hohenadel's start year is unclear ('194?'). No rental or closure information found. Do not confuse with the Oregon Table Rock Lookout on the NHLR (/lookouts/us/or/).
